issues.title: Adapter: generic ACP client
issues.body:
One adapter for every Agent Client Protocol agent (Gemini CLI, Goose, Devin, OpenCode, Claude/Codex via their ACP adapters). Implements ACP v1; v2 is tracked separately.

### Tasks
- [ ] Use official ACP TS SDK (`@agentclientprotocol/sdk`)
- [ ] stdio transport: newline-delimited JSON-RPC, stderr captured to the Worker log
- [ ] Capability negotiation → capability flags (fork only if `sessionCapabilities.fork`, marked unstable; live usage only if the agent sends `usage_update`)
- [ ] Cancel flow: `session/cancel`, answer pending `session/request_permission` with `cancelled`, map `stopReason: cancelled` (or `-32800`) to a cancelled turn, not an error
- [ ] Permission options → Decision (`allow_once`, `allow_always`, `reject_once`; Gemini's reject option id is `cancel`)
- [ ] Model switch via the config option with category `model` (no `session/set_model`)
- [ ] Per-session MCP injection via `session/new.mcpServers` with headers
- [ ] Configurable command per agent
- [ ] Auth default: API key only. Launch `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` with `--hide-claude-auth` and `@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp` with `NO_BROWSER=1`; never call ACP `authenticate` with a subscription method (owner decision 2026-11-09; #65 stays open)
- [ ] Keep the prompt-turn code isolated so an ACP v2 path can be added later
- [ ] Borrow (ADR-001): Generic `acp:<slug>` registry so any ACP agent can be added by config (Omnigent `docs/AGENT_YAML_SPEC.md` §Custom ACP agents)
- [ ] Write the worker's MCP config (which holds its token) outside the worktree at mode 0600, and delete it when the session closes; test it is never inside the repo (owner decision 2026-11-09)

### Acceptance criteria
- Gemini CLI passes conformance suite over ACP
- Cancel and permission flows are covered by recorded fixtures (see docs/adapters/spikes/61-acp, 63-gemini)
- Subscription auth methods are never selected by default (test)

_See docs/adapters/capability-matrix.md (ACP section), docs/adapters/spikes/61-acp, 62-acp-adapters, 63-gemini, and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md._

- [ ] Return a fast 404 for `/.well-known/*` (Codex probes OAuth discovery, #68)

- [ ] Per-tool policy gating
- [ ] Three-client conformance test: an MCP SDK v2 client on 2026-07-28, an SDK v1 client on 2025-era, and Claude Code as a real vendor worker

issues.title: Local auth module: token file, tacet/hello, Host/Origin checks, one-time-code browser login, per-worker MCP tokens
issues.body:
Build the local auth module that every Tacet daemon (Conductor and Mini-conductors) uses. This is ADR-003 follow-up 2. It is security-sensitive, so it needs a reviewer pass before merge.

### Tasks
- [ ] Token file: 256-bit token from crypto.randomBytes, written with pid, port, protocolVersions and startedAt to `~/.tacet/run/` at mode 0600; rotated on every start; never logged or put in events
- [ ] `tacet/hello` handshake: negotiate protocol versions (close with 4406 when none match); any other first method closes the socket with -32600
- [ ] Host and Origin checks on every HTTP and WebSocket request (127.0.0.1, [::1] or localhost with the server port); failures close with 4401 or return 401/403
- [ ] One-time-code browser login: `tacet open` passes `#code=`; `POST /auth/session` exchanges a single-use code (60 s lifetime) for an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict session cookie
- [ ] Per-worker MCP tokens bound to {workerSessionId, taskId}, injected into the worker's MCP config, revoked when the session closes
- [ ] Bind 127.0.0.1 and ::1 on an OS-assigned port by default
- [ ] Reviewer pass (`reviewer` agent) before the PR is opened

### Acceptance criteria
- A request with a wrong Host or Origin is rejected, including the DNS-rebinding case
- A socket whose first frame is not `tacet/hello` is closed
- A one-time code works once and expires after 60 s
- A worker token cannot act on another task or session, and is rejected after revocation
- No token value appears in logs, events or test snapshots

_See docs/adr/003-wire-protocols.md §3, §5, §6 and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §6._

issues.body:
Land the branches of parallel Worker sessions through a merge queue. The queue batches verified branches, runs verification on each batch, and bisects a failing batch to find the bad branch. The idea is borrowed from Gas Town's Refinery (`docs/design/architecture.md`, Merge Queue). Tacet reimplements it in TypeScript and does not port code (ADR-001). This is ADR-001 follow-up 5, and it relates to #19.

### Tasks
- [ ] Per-repo queue of verified Worker branches, in completion order
- [ ] Batch branches onto the target branch in a scratch worktree and run the repo's verify commands from `.tacet/tacet.yaml`
- [ ] On batch failure, bisect to isolate the failing branch and return it to its task as a verification failure
- [ ] Record each queue step as events (`task.*` and `worker.*`), not ad-hoc state
- [ ] Repo config for maximum batch size and verify timeout

### Acceptance criteria
- In a batch of three branches where one fails verification, the two good branches land and the bad one goes back to its task
- In a batch of eight with one bad branch, bisection after the failed batch run isolates it in at most 3 verification runs
- Queue state survives a mini-conductor restart (rebuilt from the event log)

issues.body:
The owner decided on 2026-11-09 that browser auth must not use cookies: a cookie on 127.0.0.1 reaches every local server on that host, including dev servers a Worker starts (see the ADR-003 §3.4 addendum). This replaces the session cookie in the #77 auth module (`exchangeCode`, `sessionCookie`, `readSessionCookie`). Security-sensitive: a `reviewer` agent pass is required before the PR.

### Tasks
- [ ] `POST /auth/session` exchanges the one-time code for a browser session token (256-bit, stored as a hash, capped like today's sessions); no `Set-Cookie`
- [ ] `HelloParams` for `role: "ui"` carries the browser session token; `HelloGate` validates it before opening
- [ ] HTTP calls from the page use `Authorization: Bearer <session token>`; `checkHostAndOrigin` stays as-is
- [ ] Remove the cookie helpers from `@tacet/core/node`; update ARCHITECTURE §6
- [ ] Document for the web UI (M4) that the token lives in memory only, never `localStorage`
- [ ] Reviewer pass (`reviewer` agent) before the PR is opened

### Acceptance criteria
- No code path emits `Set-Cookie` (test)
- A hello without a valid browser session token is closed; a revoked token is rejected
- The token never appears in logs, events or test snapshots

_See docs/adr/003-wire-protocols.md §3.4 addendum and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §6._

issues.title: Standalone Claude Code handoff plugin (HandoffPacket + fresh session, no daemon)
issues.body:
Owner request (2026-11-09): ship Tacet's handoff as a **standalone Claude Code plugin**, so a plain Claude Code session can hand off its context before it degrades, without running the Conductor or a Mini-conductor. This is an early, usable slice of M3 (#29, #31) built on the `HandoffPacket` schema from #5.

### Tasks
- [ ] Verify the current Claude Code plugin and hook surface from primary docs (`verify-vendor-facts`): plugin manifest, `PreCompact`, `SessionStart`, `Stop`, slash commands, and how a hook can start a new session. Record it in the capability matrix.
- [ ] A `/handoff` command that has the session write a `HandoffPacket` (goal, acceptance criteria, state summary, decisions, files touched, commands run, open questions, `nextAction`, verification). It is validated against `@tacet/core` and rejected if `nextAction` is missing.
- [ ] Automatic trigger: at a configurable context threshold (and on `PreCompact`), write the packet before vendor compaction happens.
- [ ] Reseed: start a fresh session seeded with the packet (via `SessionStart` context injection or a documented `claude` launch command). The old session ends cleanly.
- [ ] Store packets in `.tacet/handoffs/` (git-ignored by default), never with secrets; reuse the redaction rules.
- [ ] Packaging: an installable Claude Code plugin from this repo, with a short README.
- [ ] Later, sharing code with #31 so the daemon path and the plugin path produce identical packets.

### Acceptance criteria
- In a recorded fixture session, the plugin writes a valid HandoffPacket at the threshold, and a new session starts with it as context
- A packet without `nextAction` is rejected
- No token or secret appears in a packet (test)

_See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §2.3, issues #29–#32, and the `session-handoff` skill._

issues.title: Per-session model, effort and context-size selection
issues.body:
Owner request (2026-11-09): Tacet should choose, for each Worker session, the model, the reasoning effort and the context size, instead of a fixed tier per repo. Today `tiers.*` in config sets `adapter`, `model` and `effort` statically. `SessionOptions` carries only `model`, and `send()` can switch the model mid-session where `capabilities().modelSwitch` allows it.

### Tasks
- [ ] Verify each vendor's controls from primary docs (`verify-vendor-facts`) and record them in the capability matrix:
  - Claude SDK: `model`, effort or thinking options, `betas` for long context, `fallbackModel`
  - Codex app-server: model and reasoning effort per turn
  - OpenCode: model per message
  - Gemini CLI: model at launch
- [ ] Core: a `SessionProfile { model, effort?, contextWindow? }` type in `@tacet/core`, with `effort` as an `openEnum`. Add it to `SessionOptions` and `SendOptions`. Extend `AdapterCapabilities` with what each adapter can honour: `effortSwitch` (`per-turn` or `per-session`) and `contextSizes`.
- [ ] Effort: set per turn wherever the vendor supports it (expected: Claude SDK per message, Codex per turn; confirm in the first task), otherwise per session. The adapter declares which through `effortSwitch`.
- [ ] Policy: the Mini-conductor picks a profile from the task (kind, size, risk), budget headroom (the cost ledger) and observed outcomes. Config sets the bounds: allowed models per tier, maximum effort, and a context cap.
- [ ] Context size is a cost lever, off by default. The policy prefers a handoff at the threshold. It opts into a 1M window only when config allows it and the task cannot be handed off cleanly (e.g. one indivisible long read), and logs that reason in the `worker.profile` event. Config sets the cap.
- [ ] Every choice is recorded as an event (`worker.profile`) with its reason, so `tacet config explain` and the cost ledger can show why a session ran on what.
- [ ] Adapters: Claude SDK first (this repo's #11 adapter), then Codex. Each adapter declares its support honestly and the conformance suite checks it with a new P1 probe.
- [ ] Docs: the ARCHITECTURE §cost tiering section and the config reference.

### Acceptance criteria
- A task can run with a profile chosen by policy, the chosen profile is visible in the event log, and the adapter applies it (verified against the mock API by the model and effort sent).
- A profile outside the configured bounds is refused before launch.
- An adapter that cannot honour a field reports this through its capabilities instead of silently ignoring it.
- With `effortSwitch: per-turn`, a turn-level effort change reaches the vendor on that turn (checked against the mock API); with `per-session`, it is refused or applied at the next session, as declared.
- With default config, no session opts into a 1M window; a handoff happens at the threshold instead. When config allows it and the task is marked as not cleanly handoff-able, the 1M window is used and the `worker.profile` event records why.

### Owner decisions (2026-11-09)
- Effort is per turn wherever the vendor supports it, per session otherwise; adapters declare which (`effortSwitch`).
- Context size is a cost lever, off by default: hand off at the threshold first; opt into a 1M window only when config allows it and the task cannot be handed off cleanly, with the reason logged in `worker.profile`. Config sets the cap.

_See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (tiers, budget), docs/adapters/capability-matrix.md §7, and #29–#32 (handoff)._

issues.title: Sweep stale Worker MCP config files at startup
issues.body:
Follow-up from #11. Each Worker's MCP config (with its per-worker token) is a 0600 file in `~/.tacet/run/mcp/<session-id>.json`, deleted when the session closes. If the Mini-conductor is killed (SIGKILL, crash, power loss), files stay behind. Their tokens are revoked because tokens rotate on restart, but the files should not accumulate. Several Mini-conductors can share the directory, so a sweep must only remove files no live process owns.

### Tasks
- [ ] Record the owning Mini-conductor in each file's name or a sidecar (e.g. `<mini-pid>-<session-id>.json`), or keep one subdirectory per Mini-conductor
- [ ] On Mini-conductor start, remove files whose owner is not running (checked with the runtime file in `~/.tacet/run/minis/`), never another live Mini-conductor's files
- [ ] Log how many files were removed, never their contents

### Acceptance criteria
- A test leaves a file from a dead owner and one from a live owner; startup removes only the dead owner's file
- No file content or token appears in logs

_See packages/adapters/claude-sdk/src/mcp-config.ts and docs/adr/003-wire-protocols.md §3 and §6._

issues.title: Scrub Worker tokens split across streamed message deltas
issues.body:
Follow-up from #11. Adapters scrub each emitted event of the session's literal secrets (MCP header values) and known key formats. A token the model echoes can arrive split across two `message.delta` events, and per-event scrubbing then misses it. Unlikely, since the model would have to echo the token, but the event log is durable.

### Tasks
- [ ] In the Claude adapter, hold back a short tail of each delta (the longest secret's length minus one) and scrub across the join before emitting; flush the tail at turn end
- [ ] Move the helper to `@tacet/core` so every adapter (Codex, ACP, OpenCode, PTY) can use it
- [ ] Keep delta latency bounded: the held-back tail is at most the longest secret's length

### Acceptance criteria
- A test streams a token split at every possible offset across two deltas; no emitted event contains it, and the concatenated text equals the original with the token replaced
- Streaming still emits at least as many deltas for ordinary text (conformance `stream` probe passes)

_See packages/adapters/claude-sdk/src/adapter.ts (`#emit`) and ADR-003 §1._

issues.title: Codex Worker isolation: own CODEX_HOME, worktree git dir writable, plugins off
issues.body:
Owner decision (2026-11-09), from the #12 review (PR #115). Builds on the Codex adapter once #115 is merged. One issue because all three change how the adapter launches Codex for a Worker.

### Tasks
- [ ] Verify the 0.167.0 config keys first (`verify-vendor-facts`): sandbox writable roots for `workspace-write` (e.g. `sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots`) and how `thread/start` `config` or `-c` sets them; record in the capability matrix
- [ ] Writable git dir: add the Worker's own worktree git dir (`git rev-parse --git-dir` in the worktree) to the writable roots, and nothing else; never the main repo's whole `.git`
- [ ] Own `CODEX_HOME` for unattended Workers at `~/.tacet/state/<repo>/codex` (dir 0700, created on demand, `<repo>` as in the event log path); interactive sessions keep the user's `~/.codex`
- [ ] `features.plugins = false` for unattended Workers (no GitHub plugin sync on start)
- [ ] Document in the adapter README / capability matrix that the user's `config.toml` customisations do not apply to unattended Workers

### Acceptance criteria
- A Codex Worker in a git worktree can `git commit` without an approval request (test against the mock Responses API)
- An unattended Worker's thread state lands under `~/.tacet/state/<repo>/codex`, never in `~/.codex` (test with an isolated HOME)
- No `plugins-clone-*` directory is created for an unattended Worker
- An interactive session still uses the user's `CODEX_HOME`

_See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §6 (Codex Worker isolation) and docs/adapters/capability-matrix.md §2._

issues.title: Integrate unattended Codex Worker commits from the Mini-conductor
issues.body:
Follow-up from #116 (option B). Unattended Codex Workers commit on a detached HEAD into their worktree's own object store (`GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY=<wt git dir>/objects`), so their commits are not in the repo until the Mini-conductor integrates them. Until then the main repo's `git gc`, `git prune` and `git fsck` fail on that worktree's HEAD, and so does any `git push` *into* the repo (its connectivity check walks every worktree HEAD), so the decision's `git push <repo> HEAD:refs/heads/tacet/<task>` does not work once two Workers run (found in PR #124). Everything in the Worker's worktree and git dir is untrusted and can change at any moment: git run outside the sandbox must not load config or hooks the Worker wrote.

### Tasks
- [ ] Propose the integration mechanism and get the owner's OK (replaces the push in ARCHITECTURE §6), e.g. from the main repo: read `<wt git dir>/HEAD` as data (40/64 hex), copy the objects reachable from it into the shared store (`pack-objects`/`index-pack` with the Worker's store only as an alternate, objects fsck'd), then `update-ref refs/heads/tacet/<task>`
- [ ] Before each integration, re-check the worktree with `workerWorktree(cwd, repoRoot)` and run git with `trustedGitEnv` and `SAFE_GIT_ARGS` (`@tacet/adapter-codex-app-server`)
- [ ] Integrate after each Worker turn that committed, and before a worktree is left idle or removed
- [ ] Record the integration (commit id, ref) in the event log
- [ ] On a refused worktree, stop the Worker and escalate; never run git there

### Acceptance criteria
- After a Worker commits, `refs/heads/tacet/<task>` in the repo points at the Worker's HEAD and `git gc` in the repo succeeds
- Two Workers with unintegrated commits can both be integrated, in either order (test)
- A Worker that rewrote `commondir`, its `.git` file or added `config.worktree` gets no git command run on its worktree outside the sandbox, and no hook in the worktree runs (test)
- Corrupt or forged objects in the Worker's store are rejected, not integrated (test)

_See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §6 (Codex Worker isolation) and docs/adapters/capability-matrix.md §2._

issues.title: Submodules and nested repos for unattended Codex Workers
issues.body:
Follow-up from #116. Unattended Codex Workers run with `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY` and `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES` set, which apply to every repo the Worker touches: a submodule, a `git clone` or a nested repo inside the worktree writes its objects to the Worker's object dir and is unreadable without that environment. Decide how such repos should work (e.g. per-repo object dirs, or scoping the variables to the worktree with a git wrapper) without widening the sandbox.

### Tasks
- [ ] Reproduce with a submodule and a nested `git init` in a Worker worktree
- [ ] Propose an approach that keeps the shared `.git` read-only; get a human decision
- [ ] Implement and test it

### Acceptance criteria
- A Worker can commit in a submodule of its worktree without writing the parent repo's shared `.git`
- A repo the Worker creates inside its worktree is readable without the Worker's git environment

_See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §6 (Codex Worker isolation) and docs/adapters/capability-matrix.md §2._

issues.title: Rate-limit escalate and record_decision in the Mini-conductor MCP server
issues.body:
Follow-up from #18. A Worker can call `escalate` or `record_decision` in a loop, flooding the user's queue and the event log. Each call is attributed to its Worker, but nothing limits the rate.

### Tasks
- [ ] Per-Worker limits on `escalate` and `record_decision` (configurable, sane defaults), counted in the backend
- [ ] Over the limit, answer with a tool error the model can read; append one event noting the throttling

### Acceptance criteria
- A Worker calling `escalate` past the limit gets tool errors and no new escalations are created (test)
- Other Workers are not affected by one Worker's limit (test)

_See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and ADR-003 §6 for context._

issues.title: Prune per-Worker progress state when a Worker token is revoked
issues.body:
Follow-up from #18. The Mini-conductor MCP backend keeps per-Worker state (latest progress, the one-handoff-per-session flag) in memory keyed by Worker session. Nothing removes it when the Worker ends and its token is revoked, so a long-running Mini-conductor grows without bound.

### Tasks
- [ ] Drop a Worker's in-memory state when its token is revoked or its session ends
- [ ] Keep anything needed later in the event log, not in memory

### Acceptance criteria
- After a Worker's token is revoked, the backend holds no state for that Worker (test)
- A new Worker with a new session id starts with clean state (test)

_See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and ADR-003 §6 for context._

issues.title: Worktree manager state into the event log
issues.body:
Follow-up from the #16 review (PR #103). The worktree manager keeps per-worktree state in `.tacet-<id>.json` sidecar files that `touch()` mutates. AGENTS.md says state changes go through the append-only event log. Move worktree lifecycle (created, touched, merged, removed) to events, keyed by workspace id, and rebuild the registry from the log.

### Tasks
- [ ] `workspace.*` events (created, used, removed) with ids, never paths in forwarded events
- [ ] Registry rebuilt by a projection; no sidecar files
- [ ] Migrate or ignore existing sidecar files

### Acceptance criteria
- No mutable state files remain for worktrees (test)
- A restarted Mini-conductor finds every live worktree from the event log (test)

_See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and AGENTS.md (Events) for context._

issues.title: Clean up orphaned Worker processes after a Mini-conductor crash
issues.body:
Follow-up from #17 (architect review). If the Mini-conductor dies without closing its Workers, their vendor processes (Claude Code, `codex app-server` and their children) can keep running and writing to the worktree, and race the resumed session after a restart. The daemon cannot see them today: adapters own the processes and `AgentAdapter` exposes no process id.

### Tasks
- [ ] Let adapters report the process group of a session (e.g. an optional field on `SessionHandle`, recorded in a 0600 runtime file under `~/.tacet/run/minis/`, not in forwarded events)
- [ ] On `start()`, signal stale process groups that belonged to this repo's previous daemon before resuming, guarding against pid reuse

### Acceptance criteria
- After a simulated crash, no Worker process from the previous run is alive when the resumed session starts (test with a real adapter against its mock API)

_See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §6 and ADR-003 §3.2._

issues.title: Verify that resumed Worker sessions pick up a new MCP URL and token
issues.body:
Follow-up from #17. After a restart the Mini-conductor's MCP port and every Worker token change, and the daemon passes the new `mcpServers` together with `resume`. Whether each vendor honours a changed MCP server config on a resumed session is a vendor fact that is not verified yet (Claude Agent SDK `resume`, Codex `thread/resume` with `config.mcp_servers`).

### Tasks
- [ ] Verify per vendor at the pinned versions (`verify-vendor-facts`), live against the mocks, and record in the capability matrix
- [ ] Where it does not work, fall back to a fresh session seeded with the last `worker.progress` (and the sub-task prompt)

### Acceptance criteria
- A resumed Worker can call an MCP tool on the restarted Mini-conductor, for each adapter (tests)

_See docs/adapters/capability-matrix.md._

issues.title: Resume in-flight handoffs after a Mini-conductor restart
issues.body:
Follow-up from #17 (architect review). A `handoff.requested` with no later `worker.started` for that sub-task means the daemon stopped between accepting a HandoffPacket and starting the successor session. On restart the successor must start from the packet instead of resuming the old vendor session.

### Tasks
- [ ] Detect pending handoffs when rebuilding state
- [ ] Start the successor seeded from the packet (`read_task` already returns the latest packet), with `previousSessionId` and `worker.ended {reason: handoff}` for the old one

### Acceptance criteria
- Crash after `handoff.requested`, restart: the successor session starts from the packet and the old session is not resumed (test)

_See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §2.3._

issues.title: ACP: verify API-key-only auth for claude-agent-acp and codex-acp, then register them
issues.body:
`@tacet/adapter-acp` (#13) ships specs for `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` (`--hide-claude-auth`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) and `@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp` (`NO_BROWSER=1`, `api-key` method), but keeps them out of `BUILTIN_ACP_AGENTS`: neither was run live, and with the user's real `~/.claude` and `~/.codex` present it is not verified that they use the API key and leave the user's own login alone. Codex app-server's built-in provider ignores `OPENAI_API_KEY` (capability matrix §2), so what codex-acp's `authenticate {methodId: "api-key"}` does (and whether it writes `auth.json`) needs checking.

### Tasks
- [ ] Run both adapters live against local API mocks, with an existing subscription login present in the home directory
- [ ] Record which credential each request used and every file the run wrote under the home directory
- [ ] If needed, give each an isolated home (as the native Codex adapter does with `CODEX_HOME`, #116)
- [ ] Add both to `BUILTIN_ACP_AGENTS` with conformance tests; record the facts in the capability matrix

### Acceptance criteria
- Conformance passes for both over ACP against mocks
- A test shows the user's existing login files are unchanged and unused after a Worker run

_See docs/adapters/capability-matrix.md §4, docs/adapters/spikes/62-acp-adapters and #13._

issues.title: ACP: offer fork when the agent advertises sessionCapabilities.fork
issues.body:
`@tacet/adapter-acp` (#13) declares `fork: 'none'` for every agent and refuses `resume.fork`. ACP has an unstable `session/fork` behind `sessionCapabilities.fork` (spike #61); codex-acp and claude-agent-acp pass it through (spike #62). Gemini CLI 0.67.0 does not offer it.

### Tasks
- [ ] Verify the current `session/fork` request and response in the pinned ACP SDK
- [ ] Negotiate fork per session from `initialize` and report it honestly (static `capabilities()` vs per-session support)
- [ ] Fake-agent tests for fork offered and not offered

### Acceptance criteria
- A fork is only attempted when the agent advertised it; otherwise it is refused, as today

_See docs/adapters/spikes/61-acp and docs/adapters/capability-matrix.md §4._

issues.title: Adapters: launch Workers with an environment allowlist
issues.body:
The build-adapter skill asks for Worker processes to start with an environment allowlist, but the adapters pass the user's whole environment (plus their own additions). A Worker for one vendor, or any `acp:<slug>` agent, therefore also receives other vendors' API keys and unrelated secrets.

### Tasks
- [ ] Define the allowlist in `@tacet/core` (system variables, proxy and locale settings, plus each adapter's own key variables and config overrides)
- [ ] Apply it in every adapter that spawns a process (Claude, Codex app-server, ACP, OpenCode, PTY)
- [ ] Tests that a variable outside the allowlist does not reach the Worker

### Acceptance criteria
- No adapter passes another vendor's key variable to a Worker (test per adapter)

_See .claude/skills/build-adapter/SKILL.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md._

issues.title: Mini-conductor: build Worker adapters from the effective config at startup
issues.body:
`MiniConductorOptions.adapters` takes ready-made adapter instances, and only tests construct them today.

At startup (`tacet up` or the Mini-conductor entry point), each adapter has to be built from the effective config:
- the auth route (`auth.*`);
- `agents.*` presets, as `acp:<slug>` or `pty:<slug>` agents with their `env` secret references resolved;
- the Worker environment policy (`workerEnvPolicy(config)` from `@tacet/core`, #147).

### Tasks
- [ ] Composition root that builds the Claude, Codex and ACP adapters from `TacetConfig`
- [ ] Pass `workers.env.pass` to every adapter as `envPolicy`; log dropped variable names at debug level only
- [ ] Resolve `agents.*.env` secret references into the agent's fixed environment without logging values
- [ ] Build `agents.*` presets of kind `pty` as `PtyCliAdapter` (`pty:<slug>`, #156): `command`, `env`, `ready_prompt` → `readyPrompt`, and the values resolved from secret references passed as `PtyPreset.secrets` so they are scrubbed from events

### Acceptance criteria
- A test starts a Mini-conductor from a config file and shows a Worker gets exactly the allowlisted environment plus `workers.env.pass`
- A `kind: pty` preset with a secret reference yields a `pty:<slug>` adapter whose events never contain the resolved value

_See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §4 and §6, #147 and #15._

issues.title: Keep vendor keys out of Workers' tool subprocesses
issues.body:
The Worker environment allowlist (#147) keeps other vendors' keys out of a Worker, but each vendor still hands its own key to the commands it runs: Claude Code's Bash tool inherits `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, Codex's `shell_environment_policy` defaults to `inherit = all` with the key filter off, and Gemini CLI's environment redaction is off by default (capability matrix §1, §2, §5, "Worker environment"). A test suite or script the Worker runs can therefore print the key into logs.

### Tasks
- [ ] Claude: verify `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1` live on the pinned version, including the Linux `bubblewrap` requirement, and set it for unattended Workers
- [ ] Codex: verify whether `thread/start` config accepts `shell_environment_policy` (or use `-c`), and set `inherit = "core"` plus the needed variables with `ignore_default_excludes = false`
- [ ] Gemini: verify `security.environmentVariableRedaction.enabled` and how to set it for an ACP session without the user's settings file
- [ ] Gemini: it loads a `.env` from the working directory, its parents or `~/.env`, past the Worker environment allowlist; find a way to turn that off for Workers (or document it as accepted)
- [ ] A test per adapter: a tool command the Worker runs does not see the vendor key

### Acceptance criteria
- For each adapter, a live or mock-API test shows the tool subprocess environment has no API key

_See docs/adapters/capability-matrix.md and #147._

issues.title: PTY adapter: clean up per-session Claude config directories
issues.body:
The PTY adapter (#15) gives every Claude Code session its own `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` under `~/.tacet/state/<repo-hash>/claude-pty/<session id>`, which holds the session's transcript (needed to resume it) and Claude Code's `.claude.json`. Nothing removes these directories, also when `start()` fails.

### Tasks
- [ ] Remove a session's directory when its sub-task is finished and it can no longer be resumed (Mini-conductor decides), and when `start()` fails before the session existed
- [ ] Sweep directories older than the event log's transcript retention (`events.retention.transcript_days`)
- [ ] Tests for both

### Acceptance criteria
- After a failed start or a finished sub-task, no `claude-pty/<id>` directory remains; resume of a live session still works

_See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §6 (PTY hook tokens) and #15._

issues.title: PTY presets: use resume_flag and process_name, or drop them
issues.body:
Follow-up from #15 (#156). The `agents.<slug>` preset schema for `kind: pty` accepts `resume_flag` and `process_name` (after Gas Town's agent presets), but `PtyCliAdapter` uses neither: generic presets report `resume: false` and refuse `start({ resume })`.

### Tasks
- [ ] Decide per field whether it is useful for a generic CLI; verify the flags of at least one real CLI first (`verify-vendor-facts`)
- [ ] Either support resume through `resume_flag` (and report `resume` in the capabilities only when it is set), or remove the field from the schema and the docs
- [ ] Either use `process_name` (e.g. to tell a CLI's own exit from a wrapper's), or remove it

### Acceptance criteria
- `resume_flag` and `process_name` are each either used by `PtyCliAdapter` (with a test) or gone from the schema and docs
- If resume is supported, a test resumes a fake CLI's session through `resume_flag`

_See packages/adapters/pty/src/cli-adapter.ts, packages/core/src/config/schema.ts and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §3._

issues.title: Core: modelSwitch 'none' for adapters that cannot choose a model
issues.body:
Follow-up from #15 (#156). `AdapterCapabilities.modelSwitch` has no value for an adapter that cannot choose a model at all. Generic PTY presets (`pty:<slug>`) report `launch-only` as an interim: the preset's command fixes the model, and `start({ model })` is refused with `ProfileRefusedError`, never ignored. A router reading `launch-only` may still believe it can pick a model. Human decision: add `'none'` to core, or keep `launch-only` and document the refusal.

### Tasks
- [ ] Decision recorded on this issue
- [ ] If `'none'`: add it to the core type and schema, set it for `PTY_CLI_CAPABILITIES`, and make routing skip model choice for such adapters
- [ ] Conformance probe: an adapter with `modelSwitch: 'none'` refuses `start({ model })` with `ProfileRefusedError`

### Acceptance criteria
- If `'none'` is adopted: the probe passes for `pty:<slug>` and fails for an adapter that ignores the model
- If `launch-only` stays: `PTY_CLI_CAPABILITIES` documents that `start({ model })` is refused

_See packages/core/src/adapter/types.ts, packages/core/src/testing/conformance.ts and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §3._

issues.title: Resolve keychain secret references in config
issues.body:
Follow-up from #149. Config accepts `{ keychain: "service/account" }` secret references (`SecretRef`), but `resolveSecretRef` (`@tacet/core/node`) resolves only `{ env: NAME }`: a keychain reference used by a Worker's agent is a startup error naming its config path. Resolve them from the OS keychain without the value touching disk, argv of long-lived processes, logs or events.

### Tasks
- [ ] Verify the platform tools and their exact invocation and exit codes (`verify-vendor-facts`): macOS `security find-generic-password`, Linux Secret Service (`secret-tool lookup`, libsecret); decide what `service/account` maps to on each
- [ ] Resolve keychain references in `resolveSecretRef`, returning a `Secret`; a missing item, a locked keychain or a missing tool is an error naming the config path, never a value
- [ ] Keep `{ env }` behaviour unchanged; update ARCHITECTURE.md §4

### Acceptance criteria
- Unit tests with the platform tool replaced by a fake cover found, missing, locked and tool-not-installed
- No resolved value appears in errors, logs or events (test)

_See packages/core/src/node/config/secret-ref.ts, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §4 and §6._

issues.title: Verify live how Codex and Gemini CLI scope resume to a worktree
issues.body:
Follow-up from #157. A `pty:<slug>` preset's `resume_flag` continues the CLI's last session in the Worker's checkout. That is only safe if the CLI's resume picks among the sessions of its working directory: a wider scope (a project root shared by sibling worktrees) would let a Worker continue another Worker's session. From help text only: codex-cli 0.167.0 `resume --last` is cwd-filtered (`--all` disables it); Gemini CLI 0.67.0 `--resume latest` is per "project", and whether a git worktree is its own project is unknown. Gemini is therefore not given as a `resume_flag` example.

### Tasks
- [ ] Live, against the local mock APIs: two sibling git worktrees of one repo, a session in each, then resume in one with `codex resume --last` and with `gemini --resume latest`; record which session each continues
- [ ] Record what each CLI does when asked to resume with no saved session in that directory (exit code, message, or a fresh session)
- [ ] Update capability matrix §1 ("Generic PTY presets: resume") and, if Gemini scopes to the worktree, add it back as an example

### Acceptance criteria
- Both behaviours recorded with versions and the commands used; each UNVERIFIED mark in that row is resolved or kept with a reason
- If a CLI scopes wider than the worktree, the docs say not to set `resume_flag` for it

_See packages/adapters/pty/src/cli-adapter.ts (`resumeArgs`) and docs/adapters/capability-matrix.md._

issues.title: PTY adapters: don't leave a CLI's detached background processes running
issues.body:
Follow-up from #168. On Linux, interactive codex-cli 0.167.0 starts a managed daemon (`codex app-server --listen unix:// --analytics-default-enabled --managed-daemon`, plus `codex app-server daemon pid-update-loop`; feature `daemon_auto_start`, stable and on by default) that outlives the PTY session: after `PtyCliAdapter.close` it keeps running, re-parented to PID 1. That breaks the adapters rule "never leave orphaned PTYs/processes". `-c features.daemon_auto_start=false` prevents it for Codex (verified live, `docs/adapters/spikes/168-resume-scope/`), but any CLI run as a `pty:<slug>` preset could detach a helper the same way.

### Tasks
- [ ] Recommend `-c features.daemon_auto_start=false` in Codex preset examples, and say why
- [ ] Decide how the adapter limits detached processes: its own process group or session for the CLI and signalling the group on close (a `setsid` child escapes that), a cgroup or `prctl(PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER)`-style subreaper, or documenting it per preset; verify what node-pty already does (the PTY child is a session leader)
- [ ] Check whether the Codex daemon sends telemetry during a run (`--analytics-default-enabled`)

### Acceptance criteria
- A test or recorded live run shows no process a preset's CLI started is left running after `close()`, or the docs state the limit per platform

_See packages/adapters/pty/src/cli-adapter.ts, .github/instructions/adapters.instructions.md and docs/adapters/capability-matrix.md ("Generic PTY presets: resume")._

issues.title: buildWorkerAdapters: pass repoRoot to the Codex adapter
issues.body:
Found in the review of #181 (PR #185). `buildWorkerAdapters` (`packages/mini/src/workers/build.ts`) passes `opts.repoRoot` to the ACP and PTY adapters but not to `CodexAppServerAdapter`. An unattended Codex Worker in a git checkout needs it (`workerRepoRoot`, #116): it keys the Worker's own `CODEX_HOME`, checks the worktree against the repo root before any git command, and is where #181 marks the repo untrusted. Without it, every `codex-app-server` Worker built from config refuses to start in a git checkout ("unattended Codex Workers in a git checkout need the repoRoot option"). It fails closed, but Codex Workers cannot run.

### Tasks
- [ ] Pass `opts.repoRoot` to the Codex adapter in `buildWorkerAdapters`.
- [ ] Test that a Codex Worker built from config starts in a git worktree of the repo.

### Acceptance criteria
- A `codex-app-server` Worker built by `buildWorkerAdapters` with `repoRoot` starts a session in a linked worktree of that repo (real Codex against the mock Responses API), and its `CODEX_HOME` is keyed by the repo root.

_See packages/mini/src/workers/build.ts, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §6 (Codex Worker isolation) and #116._
